notes: The money freed by the newcomers' reduced shares (~$50-60M a year at start, reported) funds the ACC "success initiative" pool, paid out by athletic performance (football CFP/bowl success, men's basketball, etc.). That gives high-performing schools such as Clemson, FSU, Miami and SMU extra money, so the ACC no longer pays equally. The March 2025 FSU/Clemson settlement added a brand/viewership-based distribution from 2025-26 (FY2026): part of the revenue is split by each school's measured TV viewership/brand value over a rolling window, so high-rated brands (FSU, Clemson, Miami, UNC) get more. Exact percentages not verified. The settlement also lowered and phased down exit fees (see legal-exit-fees-gor.md, owned by the fbs-conferences agent).
